newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-FIORENTINA THROUGH TO SEMIS BUT BOOED OFF PITCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIORENTINA THROUGH TO SEMIS BUT BOOED OFF PITCH.

text.p: Fiorentina reached the semifinals of the European Cup Winners' Cup on Thursday despite losing their home second leg 1-0 to Benfica - a match that started with the home fans staging a silent protest and ended with them booing in fury.

Fiorentina coach Claudio Ranieri, speaking for his players who have been staging their own protest media blackout for about two months, defended the supporters' disgust and described the match in one word: "Ugly".
The Portuguese, who ultimately paid the price for their 2-0 home defeat in the first leg, were dominant for much of the game and should have managed more than their solitary first half goal.
As it was, the 2-1 aggregate win ensured Italy has a representative in the semifinals of all three European club competitions.
Juventus and Inter won through to the European and UEFA Cup semis respectively earlier in the week.
Benfica took advantage of the complete silence at the Fiorentina end of the Comunale Stadium to take the lead in the 22nd minute when Edgar banged in a cross from Paulao.
The diehard fans of the Fiesole Curve were protesting against the banning of 27 Fiorentina supporters after violence in an Italian league game when the Juventus team bus was stoned.
"Silence to defend our rights" declared a banner.
The action, which the fans have vowed to repeat at every home match, lasted for the full 45 minutes of the first half and then ended in a blaze of flares and cheering.
The players' unrelated mystery media silence was maintained with none of the Fiorentina team speaking after the game.
"We are playing well. We just needed luck and a goal -- the luck Fiorentina had in Lisbon," said Benfica coach Jose Manuel, who also condemned Portuguese media coverage of his team.
Benfica, like Fiorentina, are suffering poor form in the domestic league and have been much criticised.
The match was not a pretty sight with neither team settling into a pattern and too many sloppy passes.
"I knew it would be tough but I never dreamed it would be like this," said Ranieri. "There was no unity. What happened to Benfica in the first leg happened to us here.
"Thank goodness we scored twice in Lisbon."
He said the fans had good reason to whistle, and the players, who were unhappy with the game, understood. "It was like a funeral out there, as if we hadn't won," he said.
"They have applauded us when we lost and played well. Its only fair to whistle when we win but play badly."

The home team -- winners of the inaugural Cup Winners' Cup in 1961 -- were unlucky not to pull level in the 44th minute however, when striker Francesco Baiano hit a post after a cross from former Benfica midfielder Rui Costa.
Benfica had Belgian international goalkeeper Michel Preud'homme to thank for two excellent first-half saves from Batistuta, tipping one shot just over the bar.
